reasons: Internal control and audit (2 of 4): two control/audit flags among material weakness, adverse ICFR opinion, auditor change and disagreement. The most likely pair is a material weakness with an adverse ICFR opinion, which directly raises misstatement risk. (The card gives area counts only, not F/R IDs.)

Prior-period corrections and accounting changes (2 of 3): two of restatement/revision, voluntary accounting change and segment change are present. A restatement or revision alongside control flags is the strongest single indicator that past numbers were wrong.
Financial pressure (2 of 4): two pressure flags (e.g. incentive pay tied to revenue/EPS, capital raise, covenant or going-concern issues) give management a motive to manage earnings.

Transaction complexity (2 of 8): a moderate amount of judgment-heavy accounting (e.g. over-time revenue, contract assets, acquisition, inventory write-down or concentration), which gives room for estimation error.
Numeric warning signals (1 of 4 computable): one of the Beneish, Dechow F, accruals and cash-conversion tests is triggered. This adds some support but is not strong on its own.
Mitigating: no investigations or litigation flags (0 of 3) and no CEO/CFO turnover (0 of 2), so risk is elevated but not extreme.
